das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: The upper interior surface of a space, like a car interior or a tunnel.
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.fix: remove (or merge 'roof of a vehicle' into senses[0]; the interior ceiling of a room/tunnel is 'die Decke', and the car interior ceiling is 'der Dachhimmel')
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: 'Dach' is the exterior top covering, not the interior ceiling ('Decke').

das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.quote: used metaphorically to mean a 'ceiling' in a car
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.fix: Plural: die Dächer. Do not confuse 'das Dach' (the exterior roof) with 'die Decke' (the interior ceiling of a room).
das-dach-noun-7cb119f4.why: 'Dach' does not mean interior ceiling, and the irregular umlaut plural is missing.

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.fix: Used with certain nouns to mean to ask or make (e.g., a question, a condition, an application). | to ask, to pose, to make
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: 'Eine Frage stellen' (to ask a question) is an essential everyday A1/A2 usage.

stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.quote: Stellen specifically implies the object stands on its base.
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.fix: Do not confuse 'stellen' (to put upright) with 'legen' (to lay flat) or 'setzen' (to set down/seat); all three take the accusative case for the destination.
stellen-verb-3ddeeb2a.why: The second sentence repeats note [0]; merge the contrast and remove the repetition.

letter-noun-ea13e543.quote: La palabra 'letter' tiene dos significados muy comunes: un mensaje escrito (carta)
letter-noun-ea13e543.why: Restates the senses and glosses already shown.

line-noun-f3348969.quote: Usa 'line' para hablar de personas esperando en fila (ej. en el supermercado).
Para una marca dibujada o una línea geométrica, también se usa 'line'.

museum-noun-13e50ed9.quote: donde se dice 'museo' con acento en la última sílaba
museum-noun-13e50ed9.fix: Al igual que en español ('mu-SE-o'), el acento recae en la segunda sílaba (/mjuˈziːəm/), aunque la vocal suena como 'i' larga.
museum-noun-13e50ed9.why: In Spanish, 'museo' (mu-se-o) is stressed on the penultimate (second) syllable, not the last.

name-noun-a25a0089.why: 'apellido' is not in the glosses (that is 'last name'); sense 1 is 'reputación, fama'.

name-noun-a25a0089.quote: Palabra o conjunto de palabras con que se designa a una persona.
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Palabra o conjunto de palabras con que se designa a una persona, animal, lugar o cosa.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: 'Name' applies to places, pets, and things as well as people.

name-noun-a25a0089.label: contains proper name
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Please write your full name at the top of the page.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Examples must not contain names of people.

name-noun-a25a0089.label: contains proper name
name-noun-a25a0089.fix: Por favor, escribe tu nombre completo en la parte superior de la página.
name-noun-a25a0089.why: Update translation to match the name-free example.

cough-noun-7995d2db.quote: He has a persistent cough from the cold.
cough-noun-7995d2db.fix: She gave a quiet cough to get his attention.
cough-noun-7995d2db.why: Example shows the medical condition (sense 10), not a single act of coughing (sense 9).

cough-noun-7995d2db.quote: Él tiene una tos persistente debido al resfriado.
cough-noun-7995d2db.fix: Ella tosió suavemente para llamar su atención.

door-noun-39cd983e.quote: pero también de forma figurada para oportunidades.
door-noun-39cd983e.fix: Se usa para la entrada física de una casa, habitación o vehículo.
door-noun-39cd983e.why: Note mentions a figurative sense ('opportunity') not included in the entry's senses.

hair-noun-ebe4b0af.quote: Pelo corto y fino que crece en otras partes del cuerpo, fuera de la cabeza.
hair-noun-ebe4b0af.why: In English, head hair and body hair are the same basic sense; Spanish translation splits.

hair-noun-ebe4b0af.fix: Cuando se habla del pelo en general (como el de la cabeza), 'hair' es incontable en inglés y se usa en singular ('Her hair is long', no 'Her hairs are long').
hair-noun-ebe4b0af.why: A2 learners critically need to know that 'hair' is uncountable in English.

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: En Estados Unidos se utiliza principalmente la palabra 'juice' para referirse a cualquier bebida extraída
juice-noun-ba520c0a.fix: Como bebida en general, es un sustantivo incontable ('some juice'), pero puede ser contable al pedir porciones ('two orange juices').
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Notes [0] and [1] confuse English usage with Spanish regionalisms ('jugo' vs 'zumo').

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: En España, es mucho más común utilizar la palabra 'zumo' para referirse a la misma
juice-noun-ba520c0a.fix: En español se traduce como 'jugo' (América) o 'zumo' (España).
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Explains Spanish dialectal vocabulary as if it were a usage note for the English word.

juice-noun-ba520c0a.quote: La palabra 'juice' también puede usarse de forma figurada para hablar de la energía
La energía o electricidad que hace funcionar un aparato electrónico.
juice-noun-ba520c0a.why: Colloquial slang sense ('electricity/battery power') is not essential for an A2 beginner.

laugh-verb-67b08ddd.why: 'carcajada' is a noun ('a loud laugh'), but this entry is for the verb.

laugh-verb-67b08ddd.quote: Aunque 'laugh' puede ser tanto un verbo como un sustantivo, su uso principal es para
laugh-verb-67b08ddd.fix: Para indicar de qué o de quién se ríe alguien, se usa con la preposición 'at' ('laugh at someone/something').
laugh-verb-67b08ddd.why: Restates the gloss; a note on the required preposition 'at' is much more useful.

train-noun-a4d69b7d.quote: Una serie de personas, animales o cosas que se mueven en fila o seguidos.
train-noun-a4d69b7d.why: Too literary/rare for an A2 beginner, except in the fixed phrase 'train of thought'.

train-noun-a4d69b7d.quote: como una comitiva o la cola de un vestido de novia.
train-noun-a4d69b7d.fix: Se usa la preposición 'on' para indicar que se viaja en tren ('on the train') y 'by' para el medio de transporte ('by train').
train-noun-a4d69b7d.why: Restates sense 1 and adds 'wedding dress train', which is not in the senses.

el-dinero-noun-3c721e6e.why: shortGloss includes 'wealth', which is not covered by the senses.

el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.label: place-name
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.fix: Mi hermano vive en otra ciudad.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.why: Examples must not contain names of places.

el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.quote: Any male or female person who shares the same parents as another.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.fix: (in the plural) Brothers and sisters; people who share the same parents.
el-hermano-noun-93401bb9.why: Only the masculine plural 'hermanos' means siblings of either gender; singular 'hermano' is male.
Only the plural form carries the gender-neutral meaning.

el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.quote: Used exactly like the English 'minute' for both time and short moments.
el-minuto-noun-92bc424a.why: Filler note that only restates the two senses.
'Minute' is the most direct and common English gloss for this sense too.

el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.quote: Note that 'museo' is masculine, so use 'el' or 'un'.
el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.why: Restates the gender and article already shown in the entry.

el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.quote: In Spain, you might hear people use the plural 'museos' if they are visiting a
el-museo-noun-1ed8aff0.why: Trivial filler stating that a regular countable noun has a plural, and includes a place name.

a-veces-adv-566ce858.quote: Used to express that an action happens occasionally but not always.
a-veces-adv-566ce858.why: Restates the definition and gloss without adding useful usage information.

a-veces-adv-566ce858.quote: Place it at the beginning or the end of a sentence for emphasis
a-veces-adv-566ce858.fix: Usually placed at the beginning of a sentence or before the verb; avoid separating a verb from its direct object.
a-veces-adv-566ce858.why: Initial position is the neutral default in Spanish, not specifically emphatic.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: To feel a very strong and deep love for someone.
amar-verb-953e673e.fix: To feel a very strong and deep affection for someone.
amar-verb-953e673e.why: Circular definition using the word 'love' to define 'love'.

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: Ella dice que ama bailar los fines de semana.
amar-verb-953e673e.fix: Ella dice que ama la música clásica.
amar-verb-953e673e.why: In Peninsular Spanish, 'amar + infinitive' for hobbies sounds like an unnatural Anglicism ('encantar' is used).

amar-verb-953e673e.quote: She says she loves dancing on the weekends.
amar-verb-953e673e.fix: She says she loves classical music.
amar-verb-953e673e.why: Update translation to match the corrected natural example.

dar-verb-7cb7de0d.fix: 'Dar' is irregular in the first-person singular present ('doy') and in the preterite ('di', 'diste', 'dio', etc.).
dar-verb-7cb7de0d.why: A2 learners need to know the common irregular forms 'doy' and 'di'.

debil-adj-3af279b9.quote: Used to describe both physical weakness and weak things like a faint voice or a
debil-adj-3af279b9.fix: 'Débil' has the same form for masculine and feminine singular, and forms its plural by adding '-es' ('débiles').
debil-adj-3af279b9.why: Note [0] merely summarizes the two senses; replace with helpful grammar info.

debil-adj-3af279b9.quote: Se escuchaba una débil luz al fondo del pasillo.
debil-adj-3af279b9.fix: Se veía una débil luz al fondo del pasillo.
debil-adj-3af279b9.why: Semantically nonsensical: 'se escuchaba' means 'could be heard', but 'luz' is 'light'.

smell-verb-908c9ead.why: 'Oler a' requires a noun; with adjectives (like the example), the translation is simply 'oler'.

snake-noun-d1d756ef.quote: En contextos informales, a veces se usa 'serpent' en literatura
snake-noun-d1d756ef.fix: En literatura o contextos formales a veces se usa 'serpent', pero en la vida diaria 'snake' es la palabra estándar.
snake-noun-d1d756ef.why: Contradictory phrasing: 'serpent' is formal/literary, not used in informal contexts.

spring-noun-5b622de6.quote: La palabra 'spring' tiene varios significados muy comunes en inglés: la estación del año, un
spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: En inglés estadounidense, a menudo se dice 'in the spring' (con el artículo 'the'), además de 'in spring'.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: Note merely restates the glosses of the three senses without adding usage information.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: There is a broken metal spring inside the old sofa.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: 'Lose its spring' means to lose elasticity (uncountable), not a literal metal coil.

spring-noun-5b622de6.fix: Hay un resorte de metal roto dentro del sofá viejo.
spring-noun-5b622de6.why: Mistranslates the uncountable sense 'elasticity' as a single physical coil, sounding unnatural in Spanish.

stomach-noun-e0b3137c.quote: The baby kicked in her stomach.
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.fix: He lay flat on his stomach.
stomach-noun-e0b3137c.why: Sense 1 defines the external front of the body, whereas a baby kicks inside.

tall-adj-9bc90422.quote: De un objeto que tiene una gran extensión vertical.
tall-adj-9bc90422.why: Tallness of people and vertical objects are the same core meaning; notes already explain usage.

rico-adj-44bbcf17.quote: Do not confuse this with 'rico' in a social context, which can sometimes imply
rico-adj-44bbcf17.fix: Remove, or note that colloquially '¡qué rico!' can also mean cute, nice, or pleasant.
rico-adj-44bbcf17.why: Confusingly tells the learner not to confuse the word with itself in a minor shade.

tarde-adv-d70fcb11.why: Includes the noun meaning 'afternoon', which is not in the adverb senses.

tarde-adv-d70fcb11.quote: Used as an adverb meaning 'late', as in 'Llego tarde' (I am arriving late).
tarde-adv-d70fcb11.fix: Do not confuse the adverb 'tarde' (late) with the feminine noun 'la tarde' (the afternoon/evening).
tarde-adv-d70fcb11.why: Only restates the part of speech and gloss; should contrast with the noun 'la tarde'.

el-tomate-noun-f75defb5.quote: In Spain, the word 'tomate' is used for both the fruit and the processed sauce
el-tomate-noun-f75defb5.fix: 'Tomate frito' is commonly used in Spain to refer to fried tomato sauce.
el-tomate-noun-f75defb5.why: The note claims a sauce meaning that is not listed in the senses.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.quote: The way a person is dressed; clothing or attire in general.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: Using 'vestido' for general clothing ('ropa') is formal/dated and unnecessary for A2.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.quote: El código de vestido para el evento es formal.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.fix: Gasta mucho dinero en comida y vestido.
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: 'Código de vestido' is an unnatural calque; Spanish uses 'código de vestimenta' or 'etiqueta'.

el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.label: matches marginal sense
el-vestido-noun-ed96fc14.why: Remove 'attire' once the marginal second sense is removed.

la-ducha-noun-0f208a60.quote: Water sprayed over the body to wash.
la-ducha-noun-0f208a60.fix: An act of washing the body under sprayed water.
la-ducha-noun-0f208a60.why: The example ('darse una ducha') shows the act of showering, not the water itself.

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.label: place name in example
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.quote: Mi familia vive en un pueblo pequeño cerca de Madrid.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.fix: Mi familia vive en un pueblo pequeño cerca de la costa.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.why: Examples must not contain names of people, brands, or places (Madrid).

la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.quote: My family lives in a small town near Madrid.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.fix: My family lives in a small town near the coast.
la-familia-noun-b7e359b9.why: Update translation to match the removal of the place name.

la-primavera-noun-8de86356.quote: Used with the feminine article 'la' or contraction 'en primavera' (in spring) without an article.
la-primavera-noun-8de86356.fix: Takes the feminine article 'la', except after 'en': 'en primavera' (in spring).
la-primavera-noun-8de86356.why: 'En primavera' is a prepositional phrase without an article, not a contraction.

la-universidad-noun-23f53449.quote: In Spain and Latin America, 'universidad' refers to higher education institutions where you study for
la-universidad-noun-23f53449.fix: Do not confuse with the false friend 'el colegio', which means 'school' (especially primary or secondary school), not 'college'.
la-universidad-noun-23f53449.why: Merely restates the definition; a note warning about the false friend 'colegio' is much more useful.

lleno-adj-066a8598.why: Standard Castilian phonological transcription distinguishes /ʎ/ for 'll', or notes yeísmo; /ˈʎeno/ is standard.

no-expression-d81d4edd.fix: Used at the end of a statement to ask for agreement or confirmation. | right?, isn't it?, don't you?
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: Everyday tag question ('¿no?') is very common at A1-A2 level.

no-expression-d81d4edd.quote: Used as a standard negation to express refusal or disagreement.
Unlike in English, you often use 'no' twice in a sentence: one to negate the
no-expression-d81d4edd.fix: Unlike in English, Spanish uses double negatives: 'no' goes before the verb when a negative word like 'nada' (nothing) or 'nadie' (nobody) follows the verb (e.g., 'No quiero nada').
no-expression-d81d4edd.why: 'No quiero nada' does not use the word 'no' twice; it uses 'no' + 'nada'.

kupowac-verb-781f5553.quote: Muszę kupować świeże owoce na targowisku.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.fix: Zawsze kupuję świeże owoce na targu.
kupowac-verb-781f5553.why: With 'muszę', imperfective 'kupować' sounds unnatural without habitual context; 'targ' is more common than 'targowisko'.

caro-adj-b40d396d.quote: That which costs a lot of money.
caro-adj-b40d396d.why: Worded as a noun definition rather than an adjective definition.

caro-adj-b40d396d.quote: 'el precio más caro' - the highest price paid for a sacrifice
caro-adj-b40d396d.fix: In literary contexts, 'caro' can also mean 'dear' or 'beloved' (e.g., 'mi caro amigo'), though 'querido' is the normal everyday word.
caro-adj-b40d396d.why: 'El precio más caro' shows figurative cost, not the emotional 'beloved' sense.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: The noun entry 'la mañana' does not have 'tomorrow' as a sense.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.quote: A period of time or an entire day considered in relation to a specific event
la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: Duration in 'toda la mañana' is the same noun sense ('morning'), not a distinct meaning.

la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.quote: When used as a noun with an article ('la mañana'), it always refers to the time of day.
la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.fix: With the feminine article ('la mañana'), it means 'the morning'. Without an article ('mañana'), it is an adverb meaning 'tomorrow' (or with the masculine article, 'el mañana', 'the future').
la-manana-noun-87f1c2a0.why: With the masculine article ('el mañana'), it is a noun meaning 'tomorrow / the future'.

adj-0eff005c.why: shortGloss includes 'light-colored', which is absent from the senses and contradicted by note [1].

adj-0eff005c.quote: Зимой весь город стал белый от снега.
adj-0eff005c.fix: Зимой весь город стал белым от снега.
adj-0eff005c.why: Past tense 'стал' requires the instrumental case 'белым' for a temporary state.

adj-2eb76e52.quote: Use быстрый when talking about speed in movement or action, such as a fast car
adj-2eb76e52.why: Only restates the definitions of the two senses.

adj-342a5dda.quote: Used to describe people or animals that show kindness and a warm attitude toward others.

noun-06b6922b.quote: While this word is technically a noun, it functions like an adjective (adjectival noun).
noun-06b6922b.fix: Взрослый is also used as an adjective ('adult, grown-up') and declines like an adjective.
noun-06b6922b.why: As a noun it functions syntactically as a noun, though it declines like an adjective.

noun-06b6922b.quote: It is the standard, neutral way to refer to someone who is not a child.
noun-06b6922b.why: Restates the definition and the register field.

noun-0a176f48.fix: Has a fleeting vowel in declined forms (e.g., genitive кашля) and is usually singular only.
noun-0a176f48.why: Learners need to know about the fleeting -е- (кашель → кашля) and uncountable usage.

noun-50664da7.fix: A motion picture or film. | movie, film, picture
noun-50664da7.why: Common everyday meaning ('motion picture / film', e.g., кинокартина, лучшая картина).

noun-63b38367.quote: A container of cloth or plastic you carry things in.
noun-63b38367.fix: A flexible container of leather, cloth, or plastic used for carrying things.
noun-63b38367.why: Handbags (сумки) are very commonly made of leather, which the current definition excludes.

noun-6a6386e1.why: Standard broad Russian IPA typically writes the affricate with a tie bar or consistent notation.

noun-83a7e7c6.why: Uses Polish letter 'ł' instead of IPA /l/ (or [ɫ]), and final unstressed vowel is /ə/.

verb-843f487d.quote: to eat; to drink; to suffer
verb-843f487d.fix: to eat; to take (medicine); to suffer
verb-843f487d.why: In standard Mandarin, 吃 is not a general word for 'to drink'.

verb-843f487d.quote: Besides food, 吃 is used for drinks that involve a spoon or are considered meals,
verb-843f487d.fix: Besides food, 吃 is used for taking medicine (吃药), even in pill form, and for soup or porridge in some regions (吃汤, 吃粥).
verb-843f487d.why: Neither medicine (吃药) nor noodles (吃面) are drinks.

verb-843f487d.quote: To consume a liquid or take medication.
verb-843f487d.fix: To take medicine, or to consume certain non-solid items.
verb-843f487d.why: Standard Mandarin uses 喝 for liquids; 吃 here mainly covers medicine (吃药) or soup/milk idioms.

noun-f29d6dec.quote: In Russian culture, the uzhin is typically the main meal of the day
noun-f29d6dec.fix: In Russian culture, 'обед' (midday meal) is traditionally the main meal, while 'ужин' is the evening meal.
noun-f29d6dec.why: Traditionally in Russian culture, обед (midday meal) is considered the main meal, not ужин.

noun-f29d6dec.fix: Use the preposition 'на' for what is served ('на ужин' — for dinner) and 'за' + instrumental for 'at dinner' ('за ужином').
noun-f29d6dec.why: A2 learners need the common prepositional collocations for meal nouns.

verb-0851f175.quote: to take; to catch; to rent
verb-0851f175.why: 'to catch' is not in any of the entry's senses or glosses.

verb-0851f175.fix: Has an irregular present-tense stem with a fleeting vowel: я беру́, ты берёшь, они беру́т. Past tense stress shifts in the feminine: брал, брала́, бра́ло, бра́ли.
verb-0851f175.why: The irregular present stem (бер-) and past feminine stress are essential for beginners.

verb-0851f175.fix: Он всегда берёт книги с этой полки.
verb-0851f175.why: Uses the suppletive perfective 'взял' instead of a form of the headword 'брать'.

verb-0851f175.quote: He took the book from the table.
verb-0851f175.fix: He always takes books from this shelf.
verb-0851f175.why: Update translation to match the corrected imperfective example.

verb-0851f175.quote: Мы решили взять машину напрокат на выходные.
verb-0851f175.fix: В отпуске мы обычно берём машину напрокат.
verb-0851f175.why: Uses the suppletive perfective 'взять' instead of a form of the headword 'брать'.

verb-0851f175.quote: We decided to rent a car for the weekend.
verb-0851f175.fix: On vacation we usually rent a car.
verb-0851f175.why: Update translation to match the corrected imperfective example.

verb-62298af6.quote: This verb describes carrying something by holding it or wearing it as you move somewhere.
verb-62298af6.fix: 'Нести' is a unidirectional verb of motion (carrying something in one direction right now). Its multidirectional pair is 'носить' (carrying habitually or in various directions), and its perfective is 'понести'.
verb-62298af6.why: 'Нести' does not mean 'to wear' (that is 'носить'), and the motion-verb pair is missing.

verb-ac9e5c2f.quote: Followed immediately by the instrumental case (in Russian, nouns take the ending -е or -ой).
verb-ac9e5c2f.fix: Takes the preposition 'в' followed by the prepositional case (e.g., нуждаться в помощи — to need help).
verb-ac9e5c2f.why: 'Нуждаться' governs 'в' + prepositional case, not the instrumental case without a preposition.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: The first consonant of the second syllable is voiceless /k/, not voiced /ɡ/.

bakmak-verb-3fe06595.quote: Bakmak is a very versatile verb. While its primary meaning is to look, it is
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.fix: 'Bakmak' takes the dative case (-(y)e/-(y)a) for the person or thing looked at or cared for.
bakmak-verb-3fe06595.why: Restates the senses; a note should instead state that 'bakmak' governs the dative case.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: To remain inactive, dormant, or unresponsive.
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Figurative/idiomatic use not needed at A2; 'uyumak' is simply 'to sleep'.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: Proje üzerinde çalışanlar biraz uyudu ama şimdi tekrar hızlandılar.
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Unnatural Turkish; saying workers 'slept' sounds like they literally napped or is rude slang.

uyumak-verb-56fff049.quote: Uyumak is the standard verb for sleeping, but it can also describe mechanisms or systems
uyumak-verb-56fff049.fix: Do not confuse 'uyumak' (to sleep, intransitive) with 'uyutmak' (to put to sleep, transitive).
uyumak-verb-56fff049.why: Restates the senses and teaches a marginal usage instead of useful A2 grammar/vocabulary.

noun-8c1fb7b7.fix: The vowel е is fleeting and drops in all other forms: незнакомца, незнакомцы.
noun-8c1fb7b7.why: Has a fleeting vowel 'е' in all declined forms, which beginners need to know.

noun-91420c9c.why: Unstressed pretonic 'о' reduces to [ɐ], not [a], in standard Russian IPA.

noun-980d1ea3.fix: To say 'by plane', use на самолёте (literally 'on a plane') or the instrumental самолётом.
noun-980d1ea3.why: Preposition 'на' for transport (на самолёте) is essential usage for A2 learners.

noun-c32f2ada.quote: In Russian, 'море' refers specifically to the sea. Be careful not to confuse it with 'озеро'
noun-c32f2ada.fix: Takes the preposition на (not в) when talking about going to or being at the seaside: ехать на море, отдыхать на море.
noun-c32f2ada.why: Restates the gloss; should instead explain the use of preposition 'на' (на море).

noun-c32f2ada.quote: Metaphorically, 'море' can be used to describe a vast quantity of something
noun-c32f2ada.fix: In the plural, the stress shifts to the ending: моря́ (seas), морей.
noun-c32f2ada.why: Merely repeats sense 1; better to note the plural stress shift (мо́ре -> моря́).

noun-d65f1aed.quote: Used for both physical pain and emotional suffering.
noun-d65f1aed.fix: Feminine third-declension noun ending in a soft sign (-ь); its genitive, dative, and prepositional singular forms are боли.
noun-d65f1aed.why: Just repeats the two senses; noting the soft-sign feminine declension is much more useful.

ask-verb-1acc9c10.why: 'Interrogar' means to interrogate, which is too formal/specific for 'ask'.

box-noun-fb138ba4.quote: La palabra 'box' se refiere principalmente a una caja con lados planos, pero también puede
box-noun-fb138ba4.fix: Forma el plural añadiendo '-es': 'boxes'. En formularios o pantallas, 'box' también se refiere a una casilla para marcar o escribir (por ejemplo, 'check the box').
box-noun-fb138ba4.why: Note merely restates the definitions without adding useful grammar or usage information.

box-noun-fb138ba4.fix: Cuadro o espacio pequeño en una página o pantalla para escribir o marcar una opción. | casilla, recuadro
box-noun-fb138ba4.why: Missing the common A2 everyday sense of a checkbox or text box on a form/screen.

busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: shortGloss should cover both senses, including 'concurrido' for sense 1.

busy-adj-c3c2275e.quote: Usa 'busy' para describir a una persona que tiene mucho trabajo o una agenda llena.
busy-adj-c3c2275e.fix: Aunque se escribe con 'u', la primera sílaba se pronuncia con sonido de 'i' corta (/ˈbɪzi/). También se usa para líneas telefónicas ocupadas ('the line is busy').
busy-adj-c3c2275e.why: Note [0] merely restates sense [0]. Pronunciation and telephone usage are much more helpful.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Se usa tanto para el contacto telefónico como para gritar el nombre de alguien desde
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: Para decir cómo se llama alguien o algo, se suele usar en voz pasiva: 'It is called...' (Se llama...), en lugar de traducir 'se llama' literalmente con 'calls itself'.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: Note merely repeats the senses instead of giving useful usage advice.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: Por favor llama su nombre para que nos escuche.
call-verb-724aa94d.fix: Por favor, di su nombre en voz alta para que nos escuche.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: 'Llamar su nombre' is an unnatural calque in Spanish.

call-verb-724aa94d.quote: They call the new park Green Valley.
call-verb-724aa94d.why: Examples must not contain place names (and 'Max' should be avoided too: use a nickname/noun).
